JOURNEY TO THE WEST AND WEST SPIRITS

Master, listening to your analysis and assessment of the story Bach Xa, I feel it makes a lot of sense. Currently, I still have a few questions to ask the assistant professor: Journey to the West is a famous series that is very popular with the masses, has been made into a movie and has been welcomed by many people...

But when I was young, watching the movie, I felt Tang Tang was too cowardly and weak... Why did Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara tell Sun Wukong to worship him as his teacher? Furthermore, he also passed on the Co mantra to Duong Tang to punish those who specialize in "punishing evil and bringing good" like Ton Dai Thanh? Tang Tang is not more talented, how can he educate his disciples? How should this story be explained from the Buddhist point of view?

Venerable Dieu Phap replied:

– I think that if you understand Buddha's teachings, you should explain Journey to the West like this:

As mentioned in the book, the Tang Monk himself followed the Hinayana dharma, so Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara appeared as an old monk, giving advice and advice to the Tang Monk that he should go to the West to visit the Buddha and request the Mahayana sutras.

The path to Tay Thien to request sutras is actually the path that Huyen Trang practiced, saving himself and others. But the path of practice is never flat, always full of difficulties and dangers.

The three disciples following Duong Sang represent three types of evil: greed, anger, ignorance, of every living being. Pigsy represents people with serious greed: greed for wealth, greed for beauty, greed for fame, greed for profit, greed for food, greed for sleep... That's why he was forced to keep the eight precepts, implying that only observing the precepts can extinguish desires; Only observing the precepts can attain wisdom, so it is called Enlightenment.

Sun Wukong represents those who act responsibly, are talented, but have great anger! Giving the name Wukong is to warn these types of people to clearly understand the morality: “All impermanence, all dharmas are empty”.

As for Sa Ngo Tinh, he refers to people who are honest and kind but stupid. Because they do not understand Buddha's teachings, they commit many crimes of karma (eating meat and killing people). He used to live in Luu Sa River, specializing in eating human flesh. Naming Ngo Tinh means he wants him to practice pure conduct. If he wants to escape the three worlds, he needs to be compassionate and not kill.

Tang Sangha is a master, looking at the four great stages of emptiness, he is not seduced by wealth, beauty, fame, or fortune. Although he is not as good at magic as his disciples, but in the moments close to the brink of life and death, facing the matter of life and death, he still takes it lightly and declares:

"It's better to take one step forward towards the West and die, than to not retreat to live" - when Wukong broke the law and disobeyed his teacher, he was forced to recite the mantra carefully. This implies that: Use precepts to restrain him and make him change his ways.

The Tang Monk did not swear by martial arts, could not change, only knew Buddha in his mind, implying that: "The purpose of practice is not to seek magical powers."

As for Wukong, even though he has great magical powers, if he encounters a monster whose magic is too good, wouldn't he do everything he can to stop him? But in the end, evil cannot overcome justice!…

When his life is in danger, Duong Sang always thinks of Buddha, Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara will certainly support the good and bad to turn good, helping Duong Sang turn danger into peace. Besides, some of the youkai Wukong can't deal with, most of them are attendants of saints or their beastly subordinates...

This should be solved like this: Bodhisattva, the immortals wanted to help Tang Sangha quickly attain sainthood, so they deliberately created obstacles...

Everything is a test, let's see how he copes? Tang Tang, right at the gate of life and death, never blamed Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara for inciting him to go get the sutras!

Venerable Monk can ride a cloud for eighteen thousand miles, yet he cannot escape the hands of Buddha Tathagata. If the Buddha wanted to bring the Mahayana Sutras to the Tang Sangha, then this would be too easy, wouldn't he just need to lift his hand once and it would be done? Or maybe, just letting Sun Wukong go get the Sutras would reduce the trouble?...

Therefore, this Journey to the West warns us: Cultivation is very arduous. In a Buddhist study group, there are always all kinds of people who vow to seek the dharma. The Buddhist community is a great furnace of "collecting essence" that absorbs and absorbs all…..

Buddha Dharma is strong, nothing can break it, Buddha Dharma is also strong, nothing can separate it... As long as everyone always maintains mindfulness and practice, they can achieve karma together. Therefore, after thousands of years of hardship and danger, we finally met the Buddha. But it's time to enter“The Sutra Pavilion”getting the book but encountering obstacles, this is meant to say: "As long as you have not become a Buddha, you are still ignorant", also explains: "If you let go, then you can do it."

On the way back, all the Buddha scriptures fell into the water, in the end only six words remained “Namo Amitabha Buddha! In the "Vajra Sutra" Buddha also said: “If you say that the Tathagata preaches the Dharma, it means defaming the Buddha.”copper also refers to: at the end of the dharma later on, all the scriptural texts that once existed will gradually disappear, first the “Surangama Sutra…until finally only the six words “Namo Amitabha Buddha!” only.

In fact, this type of explanation is just trying to "correct the curve to make it straight", having no choice but to do so.

But in reality, "Journey to the West" and "Phong Than" are two works that originated from the conflict between Buddhism and Taoism, caused by both sides attacking each other.

Recently, Mr. Hu Van - the star of Bac Dau Zen school - once explained the background of these two series as follows:

"That year in Beijing, Venerable Bach Van preached "Tao Te Ching" at Bach Van Temple. Many Taoists ran to listen and then asked to join the Buddhist sect and become Venerable, making the Taoist monks at Truong Xuan Quan dissatisfied, so they filed a lawsuit with the mandarin...

The court wanted to resolve the conflict between the two sides, so it ordered Truong Xuan Quan (of Taoists) to change to Truong Xuan Pagoda, and Bach Van Pagoda (of monks) to change to Bach Van Quan.

The Taoists were not convinced, so they wrote the novel Journey to the West, the purpose of which was to slander Buddhism, so viewers of Journey to the West must have wisdom and bright eyes. If they clearly understand the historical situation at that time, they will immediately see the truth.

The most dangerous thing is that, in the novel, after Tang Tang requested the sutras, when he returned to Tong Thien Ha, all the Buddha sutras fell into the river and lost all the words, in the end only six words remained: "Namo Amitabha Buddha!" This is what they want to say: Xuanzang's entire work on translating the Buddha's Sutras is fake.

Unfortunately, the world later misunderstood and fervently believed in Journey to the West, causing Huyen Trang's true story of Journey to the West to be buried, distorted, and lost...

In response to the novel Journey to the West, the Venerable also "returned the favor", they wrote "Phong Than Bang" to insult the Taoist. Looking from this point of view, you will realize that everywhere in the story is... Damn Taoist!

For example, it is said that Taoist monks and immortals of course have the skill, but they are all executed one after another by the sword.

Viewers of these two novels, if they do not clearly understand the historical context of Buddhism and Taoism competing at that time, will misunderstand and assume that the fake is real!

CRITICAL LAYERS

The small two-story house of layperson Chan Minh was just inaugurated to the sound of crackling firecrackers. Chan Minh and his wife happily helped their 80-year-old parents into the new house. That afternoon, they held a small party (including tea, fruit juice and fruit cakes) for close neighbors who came to celebrate the housewarming. Their two-story building was the first story in the village, so it received special attention from everyone, especially three years ago, their family was among the poorest in the village, not even having a kitchen. Their kitchen is covered with two torn mats supported by four tree stakes. When it rains, the furnace (shaped by three chipped bricks) gets wet...

In their entire family, there are parents above and four children below. The burden of the family falls on the daughter-in-law (Chan Minh's wife). So where is Chan Minh? Where are you going to escape responsibility?…

This must have happened since the government began reforming, at that time Chan Minh gave the land to his family to manage, and he himself became Director of the Packaging Company. At first, although he worked hard, he was able to shoulder the burden. Then, because he wanted to earn more money and do big business, he borrowed twenty thousand from the bank. Seeing that his business could make a living, the bank accepted the loan.

Having money, Chan Minh then found a partner, but not long after he was betrayed by these so-called "close friends", they "stole" the entire package of money and fled. At this time, it was difficult for Chan Minh to stay afloat, the bank collected his debt, and the court sent a warrant to his home... Chan Minh had no choice but to play the "escape" card and quickly ran to take refuge with his close friend Dan Luong in district H.

At this time, Dan Luong was planning to go to T city. to find me, because he knew that I was worshiping a high priest there as a teacher, of course Dan Luong did not ignore this good opportunity, so he took his fallen director friend (who was pretending to be Chan Minh) with him, asking me to take them to visit Venerable Dieu Phap.

Fate is truly unimaginable. Chan Minh was betrayed by his friend and ran away with all his money, thus becoming a disciple of Venerable Dieu Phap.

When he returned to Dan Luong's house, Chan Minh did not dare to stay here, because he heard that the Procuracy was sending people to find out his whereabouts. So he had to take refuge in a remote area, living in an abandoned hut and taking care of this area. Dan Luong visits once a day. Because there are no people here, it is especially peaceful and quiet. Chan Minh stayed here for eight long months. During these eight months, except for sleeping and meditating, he focused on memorizing and chanting the Shurangama mantra, living exactly like a person leaving the home life in seclusion: fasting, reciting Buddha's name, and chanting the Shurangama master (under the guidance and supervision of Venerable Dieu Phap). At night there were no electric lights, not even oil lamps were lit.

When he practiced cross-legged exercises, because he was over 40 years old, had big legs and a big belly, it was very difficult to practice crossing his thighs. Because he couldn't do it, it was very nerve-wracking.

One night, while he was struggling to practice sitting cross-legged, he suddenly saw a fat monk sitting across from him, teaching him how to meditate... and said:

– You are so fat, you can practice sitting like me!

So he imitated the fat monk, placing his right thigh on top and his left thigh folded underneath. Both hands face down, hanging naturally on the thighs, eyes slightly closed...

“Oh! The darkness has turned into a blue sky, the surroundings are vast, silent, without a sound... Where am I? Why can't I see my body anymore? But I still have thoughts and thoughts... Am I dead?

Feeling a little tense in his heart, Chan Minh quickly opened his eyes. It was already dimly lit. He clearly saw that he was still sitting, but the fat monk was nowhere to be seen... “Aren't you dreaming?”… Chan Minh looked down, checked, and saw that his legs were still cross-legged in the same position as the fat monk had taught.

“I wasn't dreaming, so why is it morning?… It was true that not long after it got dark, I started to sit quietly, then a fat monk came to teach me to sit, just for a little while?... But now it's morning? Failed… I… sit all night? But my spirit is very alert, very good, right?”…

That morning, Chan Minh was thinking endlessly, wondering, until Dan Luong brought rice, and he hastily told the story of last night. Dan Luong says:

– This region does not have any monks like you describe!

The next day at noon, Dan Luong brought food and also brought Buddha images for Chan Minh to see. As soon as Chan Minh looked, he immediately recognized the image of the Buddha sitting in the front row and shouted:

– That's right, his appearance is exactly like this Venerable, last night he taught me to sit exactly like that.

Dan Luong told Chan Minh:

– This person is Bodhisattva Maitreya, will be Buddha in the future, so he is also called Buddha Maitreya. It takes a lot of practice to be able to feel Buddha Maitreya coming to teach like that... In the future, he will definitely achieve that.

Chan Minh suddenly remembered that last night Buddha Maitreya called himself Hang Van, and said that was his dharma name... He asks you:

– So what is the dharma name?

– The Dharma name is the name given to a disciple who takes refuge in Buddha, perhaps in his previous life he was someone who left the home life, because he was very good at sitting still. Sooner or later, one day you will understand everything!

A few months later, Chan Minh, every time he meditated, he saw all sorts of realms appear, which he couldn't write down in detail (but he was not attached or arrogant, always clearly remembering what the "Surangama Sutra" taught: “If you believe yourself to be a saint, you will definitely go astray.”…

After eight months, Dan Luong reported: There is currently a director of a transportation company who needs to recruit a person who can permanently reside in Son Tay to take on coal distribution. The monthly salary was one thousand, so Chan Minh immediately took the job.

The bank employee quickly said:

Since Chan Minh took refuge with Venerable Dieu Phap, his wife, children, and parents also fasted and recited Buddha's name. In the past, the relationship between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law was not good, but thanks to this, it has improved a lot.

“In ancient times, there was a young master from a wealthy family. His mother loved him dearly and cherished him like a pearl. In addition to the nanny taking care of the young master, his mother also assigned a maid and a family member to accompany, play, and serve him. The young master was always served by these two servants, so he had warm feelings and trusted them as his own relatives.

Time passed smoothly, the young master gradually grew up, and his affection for these two servants increased, so he very lovingly tolerated them.

Therefore, this pair of male and female maids took advantage of the young master's trust and freely acted strangely. They did a lot of cunning and wrong things, often stealing his money and belongings to sell and spend, having fun... The amount of property they stole from the young master was countless. These two servants had no shame in repentance, on the contrary, their deceitful and deceitful nature became more and more evident. Together, they planned to "take a huge chunk of the young master's money and run away"... But their plan did not come true as expected...

Time passes… The samsara wheel rotates. “If the cause is like that, then the result must be like that!”… In this life, a pair of greedy servants who stole things from the young master in the past became husband and wife, but the young master was reincarnated as their child. The reason why they have to work so hard to raise their child is because they owe him so much, it's too much to count.

As for the young master's mother in her previous life, she was reborn as a grandmother in this life, still retaining the same love and care for him as in her previous life. As for the "servant" couple, for the female owner, they have now become mothers. Of course, they always obediently, never daring to argue with her. Whenever their mother speaks, they only know to obey. The respect and respect for her is always implicit in them.

Seeing that their grandmother loved their grandchild so much, they thought this was a natural thing, but later when they wanted to discipline their child, they no longer cared. Because of the bad causes they sowed in their previous lives, in this life they bear fruit and this is the evil retribution that both husband and wife have to endure!

Looking at the mother sitting and crying, I gently advised:

– You should not resent your child, and you should not hate life, but must willingly accept it. Now, having clearly understood the source of cause and effect, the two of you should sincerely repent for the sins you committed in your previous life. Because he did not fulfill his duty as a servant in the past, on the contrary, he also embezzled his master's property and appropriated it excessively to satisfy himself... Who would have thought that in this life he would still have to return all capital and profits to the owner, so the suffering is unspeakable!...

From now on, the two must come before the Buddha to sincerely repent of the past. You must definitely maintain the vegetarian precepts. Every day, for the young master of your past life, recite a set of "Ksitigarbha Sutras", use this to support and increase the blessings and blessings of people. At the same time, I must beg my grandmother to advise me: “You're an adult so you should take care of yourself and take care of yourself! If you don't live independently, in the future you will become a useless person, a waste in society!

If your grandmother agrees and advises you, your children will definitely listen. The second part must be devoted to repentance chanting sutras, fasting, repairing... If you can do that, your son will change quickly. Because I'm not inherently lazy and don't want to do it, but because I'm influenced by the influence of karma, I don't do it!

I've finished talking, the good remedy has been given, the practical application is up to you! If you can do as I advise, everything will go well!

This true cause and effect story makes my heart heavy, because I think about the present in this world: “How many families have encountered situations where their children are unfilial, do drugs, live in seclusion, or sit all day and night in internet cafes without wanting to go home? Scenes of falling in love early and then having an abortion, not being married and then quickly cohabitating and living together... Except for the influence of wrong education and bad circumstances, is there a cause and effect that contributes to it? I think, as parents, we should check ourselves when we encounter similar situations of disobedience.”…

Because of creating evil karma, many sufferings will come... so we all need to make a vow: Life after life, keep the five precepts, practice the ten virtues, fulfill your duty, be neither greedy nor seek, not selfish or self-seeking.

We must know that we are diving in the six paths, constantly spinning samsara in the sea of suffering of life and death, and from there we become friends, create resentment, owe debts, repay debts... In fact, you cannot hide forever, you cannot escape the network of cause and effect that is spread very intimately and delicately in heaven and earth!

Only by receiving the Buddha's teachings and following them can we hope to one day achieve liberation.

KILLING OF THE FOX IS REPORTED

This story was told by my grandmother. With her permission, I would like to write it down to share with you old readers. You must "absolutely stop doing evil and focus on doing good things". The characters told in the story are all real and were witnessed by my grandmother. Here is my grandmother's original story:

“In 1951, Beijing was just liberated. At that time, I was about 5-6 years old, living with my father outside Vinh Dinh Mon. Vinh Dinh Mon at that time was still a remote wilderness area. Opposite our house is the Tat family, a couple and their children and grandchildren living together.

At that time, there were many apple trees behind their house. I often went there with my children to play and pick apples to eat.

One day I heard Mr. Tat boast: Behind his house, a fox appeared, and he decided to make a trap to catch the fox.

In less than a few days, I heard that Mr. Tat had caught the fox. Furthermore, he also peeled its skin alive to make a scarf.

A few days later, I went to Mr. Tat's house to play. As soon as I entered the yard, I immediately met aunt Bien, Mr. Tat's neighbor.

She said:

- Mr. Tat is sick and can't walk anymore!

I immediately ran straight inside, at this time his son and grandson were standing next to the bed taking care of him.

It's strange, Mr. Tat is normally a muscular man, over one meter seven meters tall, but now looking at him lying on the bed, shrunk to only about seven or eighty centimeters, moreover his whole body trembled, his face was also deformed, his mouth struggled to stammer but couldn't say anything. Listen to what his family members have to say:

- That day he was still screaming and howling very pitifully...

When we kids heard that, we were so scared that we gathered together and ran away.

That was the last time I saw old Tat, because a few days later he passed away. It is said that when he died, his body was dry, his hands and feet were like a fox, and his face was like a fox.

His family did not shroud him in a coffin, just put him in a wooden box. Listen to the neighbor named Bien tell:

- That night he died, there were many pools of urine gathering in his yard, screaming and jumping"...

After listening to the story, I asked:

– Did you remember wrongly and tell the story inaccurately?

She replied:

– Absolutely not! This terrible incident always haunts her, deeply imprinted in her mind. All her life she could not forget the sight of Mr. Tat lying sick in bed!

My grandmother continued to tell the following story:

THE EIGHTH BRIDE

In 1965, I was 18 years old, joined the Youth Union, and was stationed in the Hoang Duong area of Mongolia. In the village, near our team, there is a family named Pham. The Pham family has an eldest son and a youngest daughter. Mr. Pham married a wife from Shaanxi (I don't remember her name) who was an orphan, had lived with his brother and his wife, had a gentle personality, and was very courageous and upright.

Pham Lang and his wife have a very close relationship. But because she had been married for a long time and had no children, the bride was treated very badly by her sister-in-law (who had not yet married) and her mother-in-law. They often called the cat and scolded the dog; to insinuate, to say harsh and sarcastic words, implying: "Our family has no blessings and mistakenly brought in something that doesn't know how to give birth!".

They often mistreat their brides, feeding them only leftovers. When Tet comes, it is not allowed to make new clothes, but this bride is gentlehipsDoan – a simple translator, never argued back, she endured all cruel abuse very well.

A few years later, when her sister-in-law was about to get married, her mother-in-law harshly told her daughter-in-law:

– You are an unlucky thing! You are forbidden from attending my daughter's wedding!

She criticized and insulted me all the time... This made the daughter-in-law very sad. Finally, she couldn't bear it anymore. She angrily drank poison and committed suicide. Then she crawled out from her room, and when she reached the door of her mother-in-law's room, she died.

Her mother-in-law was so scared when she saw that, she quickly went to find a witch and asked her to enchant her. The witch said that this daughter-in-law was a poor person. After she was shrouded, she had to use big, long iron nails to hammer into her hands and feet, and stuff rocks into her mouth and press on her chest... to pacify her, making it impossible for her to ever get up and return... Otherwise, the whole family will be harassed!

The mother-in-law immediately ordered a blacksmith to make many large, long iron nails... then put it on the bride's body, then put a rock in her mouth and press it on her chest, then bury the body in the ground.

When her brother and his wife came to visit, they asked why their sister died? The Pham family explained in a roundabout way, constantly disparaging the daughter-in-law as a vile girl... Because he and his wife had little education and didn't know much, they had to endure it. The Pham family compensated them with some money and sent them back.

There is a proverb that says, "When people encounter grievances on the road, everyone around them will join forces to take action"...

After hearing about the incident, the neighbors immediately came to the Pham family and suggested: We must give the dead a satisfactory answer, we cannot let her die so unjustly and unfairly!

The Pham family was in dire need, so they had to let the neighbors take the dead man to a big hospital for examination. Results: This husband has azoospermia, so he cannot have children. It seems that the daughter-in-law was unjustly scolded and died tragically, the reason for this is completely unknown.

A few days later, the mother-in-law and father-in-law suddenly became paralyzed, he was paralyzed on the left side, she was paralyzed on the right side. As for the old blacksmith, he couldn't sleep every night. He complained to everyone:

– Every night there is a woman with her hair down standing in my house, banging dishes loudly!…

He knew that it was because of his stupidity that he contributed to his unvirtuous actions (shameful to his conscience), so he retired to his hometown in Hunan.

Not long after, I heard that he went up the mountain to cut down trees and fell to death.

Her sister-in-law's name was Kim. She used to have a strong body and ate very well. One day, she suddenly stopped eating and drinking. When she went to the doctor for a check-up, she found out that she had terminal cancer. A few days later, she died.

The daughter died, the couple became paralyzed, then on a trip back to their hometown to visit their parents, they were hit by a car and died on the way.

The husband of the unfortunate daughter-in-law, after understanding all the sources that created today's tragedy, regretted not going for a checkup sooner... So he went to his wife's grave, cried, and said sorry... He had her body dug up, removed all the nails and stones, and changed her into new clothes.

Later, the Pham family was the only one left.

As for the witch, I don't know, because this neighbor's house is near the group, so that's all I know. But surely the witch will receive the retribution she deserves.

MY TWO BROTHER

I thought for a long time before mustering up the courage to come up with a cause and effect story related to my elders. YesreasonI am a descendant and it would be disrespectful to tell stories about adults, but I hope the content of this story will help people be vigilant and deeply believe in cause and effect.

Now I would like to tell about my uncle Hai: "In my hometown, Mr. Hai was recognized by society as an exemplary good person. He was honest and loyal, but at the end of his life, he had an unfortunate ending: In 2005, he became ill and passed away.

Mr. Hai was originally a party cadre and worked hard all his life. When he was born, he held the position of Secretary of the Provincial Party Committee of the National Security Department.

He was born in 1949, used to be a member of the Provincial Executive Committee, has a righteous and honest personality. At that time, city-level leaders had just been given private cars, each with their own car and driver. Mr. Hai was also given a car, but he rarely used it; He often rides his bike to work, and the driver always has to drive behind him. Making everyone in our family laugh about this: Because he has his own car but refuses to take it, "you have blessings but don't know how to enjoy them!"...

Outside officials also thought he was old-fashioned and did not know how to adapt to the times. Because of his excessive integrity, he did not work well and was often criticized.

Then he suffered from a rare and strange disease: Blood in the stool, followed by intestinal bleeding, had to undergo many surgeries, even after not long after the surgery, he bled profusely, due to prolonged bleeding, malnutrition, multiple dissections, and severe illness to the point that everyone understood that his internal organs were exhausted and damaged...

The severe illness tormented him for 2-3 years, eventually each of his blood vessels burst and hemorrhaged, he died in extreme pain and suffering at the age of 50.

He left amid the constant buzz of public opinion. Everyone thinks: You are a rare good officer in hundreds of years, yet a loyal and honest person, a person like you who has not made any mistakes in his whole life, I don't understand why the end of his life is so sick and painful!? (While the corrupt officials who oppose him live very prosperous lives, freely enjoying pleasure and peace)... So, there is no fair cause and effect in life?...

Only later did I gradually understand all the reasons...

Because he works at the Department of National Security, he has a lot of guns and ammunition... In addition, he is very fond of hunting, he often goes to the mountains to hunt and goes down to the dam to fish...

From this, it can be deduced that for the past ten years, he has abused and killed countless lives, so he finally felt the pain and suffering... because he used available guns and ammunition to massacre many animals: causing them to bleed non-stop, their stomachs burst, their intestines burst, their internal organs exposed... This is the reason why at the end of his life he suffered from a strange and painful illness, the scene was exactly like that!”…

Having said this, I have drawn a conclusion: Even if you live with integrity and fairness; All my life I have been upright and upright, but if I have committed the act of killing, then when the retribution comes, I still have to suffer it. I cannot defend myself and escape the crime because of other good deeds...

Those who like to kill or are happy to kill, must be vigilant...

The law of cause and effect is absolutely fair, each person's situation is a projection of the karma they have created. There are evil people who have not seen retribution yet, because: In the past or in the past, they have done a lot of good deeds, so in this present life, that lucky blessing is still very great, enough to suppress bad results so that bad results cannot bear fruit (of course, the bad deeds they do do not disappear, or maybe at the same time they secretly do good deeds that we are unaware of, do not see through or do not consider them to be good deeds (for example, being filial is also considered great goodness).

Therefore, when living, you need to sow good and pure seeds, don't live drunk and dream... If you live without believing in cause and effect, and carelessly create evil, the consequences will be very tragic... Please be careful!

THE STORY MADE ME TEARS

That fall I was 12 years old, this was the most tragic time for my family: My father was seriously ill and had to have surgery, losing the ability to work. My second brother failed the university entrance exam, and my mother used the wrong agricultural chemicals, causing ten acres of growing rice to fail. At that time, I suffered from severe anemia, was barely breathing, and needed an urgent blood transfusion.

At this time, my family was overwhelmed with debt, and my mother was trying hard to figure out how to get the money to give me a blood transfusion.

While the whole family was worried about my critical illness, a neighbor named Ly walked by and seriously told my mother:

-Auntie Tu, quickly go to the back and see, your pig has given birth!

My mother suddenly woke up when she was reminded. She quickly ran to the pig pen behind her. Seeing the mother pig sticking out her tongue to lick off the blood on the piglet's body, my mother burst into tears. She was happy and grateful that the mother pig gave birth to this litter of babies, which was considered a timely rescue for her family, so she planted a Dao Tien tree near the pig barn to express her gratitude and thanks...

When my mother helped the pig give birth, she saw the sow so exhausted that she was foaming at the mouth and couldn't stop breathing... Mother knows he is old and has been enriching my family for nearly nine years... There were 16 pigs in this litter. Mom saw that the piglet was tired and quickly ordered my brother to bring her soy milk to drink. The mother pig gratefully waved her ears. She looked at the rosy and chubby piglets and told my brother:

– This time it's good, it looks like Son is saved...

But "distant water cannot put out a nearby fire", the piglets had to be raised for at least three months before they could be sold, and my illness got worse day by day. As soon as the piglet was 10 days old, I became so sick that I couldn't get out of bed. In that situation, my mother's heart was on fire, she kept walking back and forth in the house. Finally, she sighed and told my brother:

– Tuyen, go into the village and invite Vuong the butcher, I'll sell the sow to get money for Son's treatment...

My brother heard what my mother said, stood there sadly, then advised:

– Mom, the mother pig is still alive and the piglets really need milk... Although Son's illness is important, the mother pig also needs to live...

But in the end, my brother's eyes were filled with tears... I had to sneak into the neighborhood to find Vuong the butcher.

My mother quickly set up the stove, placed a large pot next to the pig pen, and started a fire to cook water...

When Vuong the Butcher arrived, he approached the pig pen, closely observed it, then sighed and told my mother:

-Auntie Tu, consider me helping you get blessings... Actually, even if I killed this mother pig, I wouldn't get much meat!

The water was boiling, my mother opened the pig pen. The sow seemed to know it, so no matter how much my mother called her with the milk cup, she still stood frozen in the barn, refusing to come out. After looking at my mother, I looked at my brother, then he kept using his tongue to lick his children who were playing and chasing each other in the cage... Suddenly, it fell over with a "bang", let out a "squeaky" sound, signaling to suckle. As soon as the piglets heard it, they rushed over to lie in rows around the mother's belly and suckle vigorously...

My mother sighed and told Butcher Vuong:

– Well then you wait! Let her breastfeed her baby one last time, okay?…

The butcher king nodded.

The piglets were full of milk and immediately spread out to play, but the mother pig continued to cry out, calling her baby to come and drink milk... It wasn't until the last pig left the mother's teat that the mother pig stood up and slowly went out. When the mother pig left the cage, she turned around and looked at her cubs with a look of longing... My mother was touched by mother pig's love, she turned away and wiped her tears... And my brother stood rooted to the spot...

The butcher king muttered to himself:

-I have never seen a sow that is so smart and has such a human-like temperament!

The mother pig looked away from her mother, then at my brother and Vuong the butcher, then suddenly she turned around, rushed into the barn and ran around the barn like crazy. My mother saw this and looked bewildered, then asked Vuong Tu Qi:

– Damn it... What do you want to do?

Mr. Vuong shook his head, showing that he did not understand...

After running for a while, everyone discovered that two rows of pig udders were engorged with milk, with streams of white milk flowing out... It turned out that the mother pig ran like that to stimulate the flow of milk, she wanted to feed her baby fully again, but even though the mother pig called out, the innocent piglets were not moved at all...

My brother was brought to tears by the mother pig's gesture. A 20-year-old young man like him burst into tears, asking for help from his mother:

– Mom, huh huh!… I beg you, mother, please don't kill the sow, okay? Son's illness, let me think of a way... hu hu!…

Vuong the butcher quietly picked up his tools and walked away. My mother, with tears streaming down her face, nodded. At this moment, the mother pig didn't let the owner waste his time calling her, she walked step by step out of the pig pen...

After that, I was saved thanks to a blood transfusion, because my brother donated blood to me.

Later, the mother pig gave birth to seven or eight more litters of pigs in our family. During the last birth, the mother pig died, the whole family cried silently, and finally the mother suggested burying it under a tree next to the pig pen...

To this day, every time we come home to visit our parents, we always affectionately look at the luxuriant tree with branches and leaves next to the pig barn and fondly remember the loving mother pig that our family once raised.

I respectfully ask everyone to be vegetarian, not to sacrifice the parents of small animals for the sake of deliciousness, or to eat their children or kill their lives...

Sincerely thank everyone.

MY FRIEND'S YOUNG UNCLE

My friends all know that I believe in Buddha. Because we are close friends, whenever they have any questions about Buddhism, they ask me, or tell me about things that happen in their family.

Today I would like to tell you a story (among my friend's stories), I hope that after reading it, you will increase your good faith infinitely.

This happened when I was in college. That day, after lunch and still having time left, I was about to go find friends to chat when suddenly I met Ms. B. She patted my shoulder and asked:

– I heard you are Buddhist?

- Right.

So B was interested in asking me a few things about Buddha Dharma. At that time, I was very surprised and excited. Surprising because: B and I were not close acquaintances, our relationship as students at school was only at the level of eating together a few times. B knows I believe in Buddha, just showing respect. Still excited: It's that B is not a Buddhist, but now seems interested in learning...

Then I asked B:

– Why do you want to learn about Buddhism? Don't you think this is feudal superstition anymore?…

So B told me a true story that happened to his uncle.

B's youngest uncle is a very virtuous person, has a noble character, is virtuous and virtuous, he strictly observes the five precepts, diligently practices, every year is like a day, and is a person greatly respected by his fellow monks.

When he was young, he went abroad to work. The emperor did not disappoint good people. In the end, he succeeded and had a glorious career. When the youngest uncle became rich, he immediately sponsored his parents, wife and children to live abroad. He has never relied on being rich and looked down on poor people. He always behaves with everyone in a gentle, friendly, and humble manner.

But a good Buddhist like you suddenly fell ill with cancer, and it was in the final stage.

This was like "a bomb exploding in the house" that shocked his relatives and no one wanted to believe it: A good person like you was met with such evil retribution! Some people even began to doubt Buddha's teachings, blaming God for not having eyes, why "do good people not receive good rewards?"...

But B's youngest uncle remained calm, because he understood that everything was cause and effect of bad karma in previous lives. Just when the doctor declared that his illness could no longer be cured... Not only was he very calm, but he also comforted relatives and friends. (Even though I can't bear to abandon my parents, wife and children, once impermanence comes, who can escape?)...

He practiced steadfastly, several decades like a day, doing good deeds and accumulating virtue, but now he has encountered this evil reward!

Everyone blames God for being unfair, but he never feels any resentment, thinking that even if he is about to die, he must take advantage of the remaining time to live well... It means treating people more kindly, trying to do more good things... Then, he single-mindedly prayed to Buddha for rebirth.

Suddenly a particularly unimaginable thing happened (right when B told it, I heard it but still couldn't believe it. But this is a real story, it happened).

One day, the youngest uncle and his family went to the supermarket to buy things. While he was walking back and forth in the supermarket, he suddenly felt dizzy and vaguely saw an old man wearing white clothes walking towards him. He picked up a fruit in the fruit row and told him:

– Eat this fruit quickly! Must eat now!

When the youngest uncle opened his mouth to ask: Why?… Then the old man disappeared. Immediately his mind regained consciousness, and he was more surprised to see the other fruit in his hand.

Uncle Ut looked around looking for… and quickly asked relatives:

– Have you seen the old man in white clothes? I just saw him clearly here but now he's gone somewhere?...

The whole family looked at him in surprise and replied that they didn't see anyone, they only saw him holding fruit in his hand and muttering to himself!

This incident was very confusing, he didn't say anything anymore, he quickly ran to the supermarket gate to buy this fruit to take home to eat. At that time he didn't think much about it.

Who would have thought that the terminal cancer that the hospital declared "curable", after he ate that normal fruit (but of unknown origin), the tumor cells completely disappeared, and the disease was thus cured.

How can this be scientifically explained?

After that strange incident, the entire youngest family began to believe in Buddha very much. We understand that thanks to Bodhisattva's compassionate blessing, he used his mighty power to save my life in the hidden gloom. This deeply touched relatives at home and abroad...

Thanks to that, I learned the story and wrote it down to share with everyone!

THE BAD NEIGHBOR

This is a story I heard from my grandmother (the person involved is still alive, and lives in the old hometown of Nantou, next door to my house). The content of the story is this:

My next door neighbor has three brothers, all disabled: One is deaf, one is mute, one is crippled. Their father was also my grandmother's neighbor in the past. It is said that he has a hot-tempered and cruel personality and likes to torture and mistreat animals. Because he gave birth to three disabled boys, he was very angry and resentful, blaming heaven and earth.

Because he was so confused, one day he went to ask the god to find out the cause. Finally got the answer like this:

“The reason is that in the past, when he was not married, his family had a pregnant sow that escaped the cage and ran away. With a violent nature, he was holding a grass knife in his hand. He immediately swung it and slashed it at the sow. The pig screamed miserably, fell down, struggled, spitting out blood, and the piglet in its stomach also bled profusely and died. It seemed like one of his knives ended several lives. Because he sowed the roots of disaster from there, today he gave birth to three disabled sons in a row."...

His deaf son (now also a neighbor in my hometown) later gave birth to three sons, two of whom were deaf and hard of hearing: There is only one normal person left, this guy knows how to be a vegetarian and worships Buddha very diligently.

It is said that as for the two brothers who are hard of hearing, their children will also have defects in their five senses and disabled limbs.

Through this story, we can see that the retribution for killing is very scary. According to my grandmother, this cause and effect story is true.

Thanh Duc Magazine No. 44-15, January 1983
